_comment: Providers the gateway serves. local: true marks a model on your own machines: it receives prompts unredacted, and a prompt the privacy rules keep at home goes only to it. strength (1 to 10) is a judgment of how good each one's code is: a vote goes to the strongest free agents, and in a build the strongest take the first tasks; edit it as experience shows who to trust (`gateway models` shows how often each sided with the majority). File order is only the fallback order for model "auto". Golden rule: free. No provider may cost money or need a card; a free API key is allowed (tier K), kept in <state dir>/keys.json or the entry's key_env variable, never in this file. A copy at <state dir>/providers.json (default ~/.ai-gateway/providers.json) replaces this built-in list, so a broken provider is a config edit, not a rebuild. kind openai: an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint (url, optional models_url and model_filter, optional key_env). kind cli: a vendor CLI run headless (bin, ask_args with {prompt}, optional model_args with {model}, optional strip regexes removed from its output). kind tty: an interactive terminal app with no prompt flag, driven through a pseudo-terminal (bin, args; see the tty fields in internal/provider/provider.go). default_model empty = the first model the provider lists. min_interval_seconds spaces calls out; daily_limit 0 = no cap known. Every cli and tty run gets its own empty scratch directory (deleted afterwards), the entry's env (an empty value removes that variable), and the top-level preamble before the prompt (an entry's own preamble overrides it); cleanup lists what the tool leaves elsewhere per run. disabled: true keeps an entry in the file without serving it.
preamble: You are answering a question for another program, which reads only your reply. Do not create, edit or run any files, and do not look for a project: there is none. Put everything asked for, including complete code, in the reply itself.

providers.note: Gemini CLI on the Google account signed in to it (/auth, Login with Google); the API-key variables are removed so it cannot fall back to a free-tier key. Only gemini-flash-lite-latest is used: on betelgeuse it answers in seconds, by hand and in a vote, while a run with no model named or with gemini-flash-latest hung until killed, three times. Ranked low because flash-lite is a small model; Antigravity gives the stronger Gemini models on the same subscription.
Claude Opus 5.5 through Google's Antigravity CLI on the signed-in Google AI Pro account. Model ids from `agy models` on betelgeuse (CLI 1.5.9).

Only opencode's own free hosted models are listed. A model is always passed, because opencode's default on betelgeuse is the local bill-the-cat. Its google/* models use an API key, so the golden rule excludes them.

Freebuff has no prompt flag, so it is driven through a pseudo-terminal. The screen tells when the reply is finished (freebuff 0.2.36 layout: the typed prompt ends with a copy mark, and a finished reply is followed by a line with the copy mark and its duration). The reply itself is read from the conversation file freebuff saves, which is then deleted; the screen is the fallback, and there a reply longer than the screen is an error, not cut short. Freebuff's own banner says it may use data for AI training.
Off: Qwen Code's sign-in (seen on betelgeuse, Nov 2026) offers only a paid Qwen subscription, API-key providers, or a custom local server. No free keyless option, so the golden rule excludes it.
Answers on betelgeuse.

Answers on betelgeuse. strip removes the notice Copilot prints before its answer saying which model it chose. The token variables are blanked so Copilot uses its own /login session: on betelgeuse it picked up a personal access token from the environment, which lacks the Copilot Requests permission.

Off: on betelgeuse `amp -x` answers Out of Credits. Amp's own announcement says execute mode uses paid credits only; its free mode, if it still exists, is interactive only (/mode free) and would need a tty entry.
--trust skips the workspace-trust prompt in print mode (it stopped the first try on betelgeuse). Answers on betelgeuse.

The Qwen2.5-Coder-7B on rigel, behind Loadout: local, no quota, 32K context. The first call after another rigel model was in use pays a model swap. Endpoint taken from Bill's ModelBackend.swift; not yet called from the gateway.
Kilo's gateway: free models need no key, about 200 requests an hour per IP. Answers on betelgeuse.
OVHcloud AI Endpoints, anonymous: 2 requests a minute per model, and reported as often rate-limited. Answers on betelgeuse.
Free key, no card: 30 requests a minute, 1,000 a day. Answers on betelgeuse.

Free key from Google AI Studio, no card; limits unpublished. Separate from the Gemini CLI's allowance. Free only when the key's project has no billing attached: a key on a billed project is charged per token. gemini-2.5-flash was refused on betelgeuse as retired; gemini-4-hydrogen goes first: it is reported to have a rate-limited free tier (Argon and Carbon are paid-tier only on the API), and the 3.8 and latest aliases follow if it is refused. Answers on betelgeuse with gemini-4-hydrogen.
Free key: only models ending :free are used, 50 requests a day. Answers on betelgeuse; its first free model is often rate-limited, and the next is tried.
Free key with NVIDIA Developer Program membership; limits unpublished. Answers on betelgeuse with the Nemotron model; gpt-oss-20b timed out there.
Free trial key: 1,000 calls a month, non-commercial use only. Answers on betelgeuse.
Free key for the flash model, one request at a time. Answers on betelgeuse.
Off: on betelgeuse (Nov 2026) Mistral's console says the Free plan must be upgraded before an API key can be created, so there is no free API tier.
Off: on betelgeuse (Nov 2026) every model answered HTTP 402 PAYMENT_METHOD_REQUIRED, so there is no free tier without a card.

Workers AI: 10,000 neurons a day free, no card. Needs the account id (shown on the Workers AI page of the dashboard) and an API token with the Workers AI permission. max_tokens is set because Cloudflare's default of 256 cut the first reply on betelgeuse short; Answers on betelgeuse.
